All 16 tests pass. Both files are rewritten:

**[confparse.py](confparse.py)** — the parser now handles every reported case:

| Bug | Fix |
|---|---|
| `;` comments not ignored | Lines starting with `;` (and still `#`) are skipped |
| Values with `=` crash | `str.partition("=")` splits on the **first** `=` only; the rest stays in the value |
| Quoted values lose inner spaces | Matching surrounding `'…'`/`"…"` are stripped after stripping whitespace, so inner spaces survive (`"John  Doe"` → `John  Doe`) |
| `[Main]` / `[main]` duplicate | Section names are lowercased and merged; reopening a section keeps its earlier keys |
| Repeated keys | Plain dict assignment — the last value naturally wins |
| Keys before any section | A `default` section is pre-created; it's only absent from the result if never used (no spurious `{}`) |
| Indented continuation | An indented line right after a key appends to that key's value, joined with single spaces (works across comment lines too) |
| Line without `=` | Raises `ValueError: line 3: expected 'key=value', got 'oops'` — line numbers are 1-based over the original text |

**[test_confparse.py](test_confparse.py)** — 16 tests: one per reported bug plus edge cases (quoted value containing `=`, continuation containing `=`, explicit `[default]` merging, malformed section header also raising with a line number).

Verified with `pytest`: **16 passed**.

All 23 tests pass. Done.

## What was wrong

The old `business_days` looped day by day (a century-wide range took ~40 s), excluded `end` from the count, and silently ignored `holidays` — the parameter was accepted but never used.

## The rewrite — [bizdays.py](file:bizdays.py)

- **O(1) counting**: full weeks contribute 5 each via `divmod(total_days, 7)`, and only the ≤6-day remainder is inspected individually — no day-by-day loop.
- **Both ends included**: span is `(end - start).days + 1`.
- **Holidays**: converted to a `set` (duplicates collapse), each checked once for `weekday() < 5` (weekend holidays are no-ops) and `start <= h <= end` (out-of-range ignored). Cost is O(len(holidays)) regardless of span.
- **Negative on reversal**: `end < start` returns the forward count negated — the same count, by construction.
- **Datetimes accepted** for `start`, `end` and holiday items via `_as_date()` (takes `.date()`); non-date types raise `TypeError` instead of failing obscurely.

## Tests — [test_bizdays.py](file:test_bizdays.py)

23 tests, all passing, including a brute-force day-by-day reference used for differential checking:

- edge cases: single weekday/weekend days, inclusive ends, reversed ranges with and without holidays, weekend holidays, duplicates, holidays on both ends and outside the range, datetime/mixed inputs, `TypeError` on strings/`None`, holidays at `dt.date.min`/`dt.date.max`;
- **full calendar differential**: `date.min` → `date.max` (~3.65 M days) matches brute force exactly;
- **100-year range** with 225 holidays matches brute force;
- **speed**: 1000 century-wide calls finish in well under a second (the old loop needed ~40 s for one such call);
- exhaustive differential over every start/end pair in a 30-day window, plus 300 random multi-decade ranges.

One test-side fix along the way: the brute-force reference itself overflowed when incrementing past `dt.date.max` on the full-calendar run — the loop now stops at `end` instead of stepping past it.
